label: Credit cards
note: Everything here comes from the issuer's MITC (Most Important Terms and Conditions) or the card's own page. Fees, caps and conditions are facts. What a card is 'worth' is not — that is arithmetic the service does from the user's own spend, shown with its assumptions. A co-branded card (Amazon Pay ICICI, Flipkart Axis, Scapia Federal) is one record under its ISSUER, with co_brand naming the partner — never a separate issuer.

network.label: Network
network.note: Not stated in most MITC fee tables — it is a per-variant fact from the card's own page. Left empty rather than guessed.

fee_waiver_spend_inr.label: Annual fee waived at spend of

co_brand.label: Co-brand partner
co_brand.note: The brand on the card that is not the issuer — Amazon, Flipkart, Swiggy, Scapia, Tata Neu, IRCTC. A co-brand is never an issuer: RBI requires a regulated bank or NBFC behind every card.

programme_partner.label: Programme partner
programme_partner.note: Fintech that runs the product experience without being the issuer — OneCard, Slice, Jupiter. The bank on the back of the card is the issuer.

conditional_benefits.shape: options[] — each with category, rate, cap, cap_period and condition

example.condition: on spends via the issuer's app

conditional_benefits.note: A benefit without its cap is a marketing claim, not a fact. Caps are required.

sanity.note: Every numeric field must be traceable to a line in the MITC. If it is not in the document, it does not go in the record.
sanity.change_log: When an issuer revises the MITC, add a new fact_version rather than overwriting. The diff is the point.
